subject: Urgent: Hosted API p99 spike after KV TTL sweep — Cargofy impact
messages:
From: Priyanka Shah <priyanka@cargofy.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@cargofy.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: API latency — p99 spike starting 10:20ET

Jonas —

We started seeing a sustained p99 increase on our hosted endpoints starting around 10:23 ET yesterday and again this morning. Baselines we typically see p99 ~ 160-220ms; yesterday it spiked to ~1.2s and we saw elevated 5xx error rate (~0.9%). Throughput briefly dropped on our endpoints as retries piled up.

We collected traces and a few example request ids and attached a zip with traces. The pattern looks like many cold KV lookups (cache-miss) followed by tokenization delays; our engineers think something may have caused a large set of prefixes to be evicted at once.

Can you confirm whether you ran any global TTL/eviction sweep or config change in the hosted control plane between 10:00-11:00 ET? This is impacting a production release tomorrow; we need an ETA.

Thanks — Priyanka

Priyanka Shah
Director, Platform Engineering
Cargofy

Attachments: p99-sample-traces.zip
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Priyanka Shah <priyanka@cargofy.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: API latency — p99 spike starting 10:20ET

Priyanka — thanks for the quick heads up and for the traces. I'm escalating this immediately.

Short answers: we did roll out a change to the TTL sweep job yesterday morning to tighten stale-prefix pruning, but it was scoped to a small shard. That change should not have caused a global eviction; I'm opening an incident and pulling infra on-call now.

Immediate next steps:
- (Rishi) can you confirm whether the TTL sweep accidentally ran at global scope?
- (Marissa) I'll coordinate with CS and propose a temporary traffic route to the smaller warm model while we investigate.
- Priyanka, can you send the few example request ids (raw request ids in traces) and confirm if you saw errors (502/504) or just latency spikes?

We'll keep you updated every 30-60 minutes until this is resolved. Apologies for the disruption.

Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: API latency — p99 spike starting 10:20ET

Jonas/Marissa — quick findings from the first-pass investigation:
- The TTL sweep job was updated to remove prefixes with last-access older than 36h (was 48h). The job has a scoped flag but due to a metrics-tag mismatch the scope evaluated to empty and ran across all hosted pools for ~7 minutes at 10:17-10:24 ET.
- That produced a high percentage of prefix evictions > 80% on some pools, which generated a warmup storm: many requests experienced KV cache-miss; the runtime reloaded KV entries and we got increased token latencies and some transient backpressure causing 502s.
- Autoscaler reacted but there is a lag; the p95 recovered faster, p99 remained elevated while KV warmup continued.

Proposed immediate mitigations (we can run quickly):
1) Revert the TTL sweep change and run a bounded rewarm job for the highest-traffic prefixes only.
2) Temporarily enable prefix-level sticky caching for Cargofy to pin hot prefixes for 24h.
3) Patch the metrics-tagging check so scope cannot evaluate to empty (hotfix).

I'm standing by to run the revert if you approve. I will attach the trace picks and a short analysis after this note.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Staff Engineer, Runtime Performance

Priyanka — thank you for the traces. We are rolling the TTL sweep revert now and will pin your top 200 prefixes for 24 hours as a stop-gap.

Jonas — can you authorize a one-time credit for Cargofy for the impacted window? They are on a mid-market contract (DFY-8423). We should also prepare an exec note if leadership wants to review.

Subject: Exec summary / ask — Cargofy hosted p99 regression (10:17–10:24 ET)

Team — brief op note for leadership review and approval for credits:
- Impact window: 10:17–10:24 ET, repeat waves through 10:45 ET as KV rewarm continued.
- Customer impact: p99 from ~180ms to ~1200ms, transient 502s (~0.9% of requests). Cargofy reports increased retries and delayed release work.
- Root cause (prelim): TTL sweep mis-scoped (metrics-tag mismatch) triggered broad prefix eviction -> KV warmup storm.
- Immediate remediations: revert TTL sweep; pin top 200 prefixes for 24h; hotfix metrics-tag guard; provide one-time credit.

Requested approvals:
- Marissa: approve one-time credit (recommendation: prorated credit for impacted window + goodwill).
- Laura: approve exec note and loop-in to Sales leadership if needed.

I'll produce a short postmortem after the hotfix and validation.

Jonas Weber

Thanks — we see improvement after your revert. p95 looks back to baseline; p99 still has occasional spikes but much reduced. We attached our SLA doc for context. We'll keep traffic steady on our canary and report if anything reoccurs.

Appreciate the fast response. Please share the postmortem when available.

—Priyanka

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: SUP-3219 postmortem draft: TTL-sweep mis-scope and warmup storm

Team — draft notes for the postmortem and planned/runbook changes:
- Timeline: 10:10–10:16 ET: deploy of TTL sweep tightening; 10:17–10:24 ET: mis-scoped evaluation and broad eviction; 10:24–10:40 ET: autoscaler ramp and partial rewarm; 10:40+ ET: revert completed, pinned prefixes, p99 returned near baseline.
- Technical root cause: the job's scope check relied on a metrics tag that was renamed during an unrelated instrumentation change; when the tag lookup failed it defaulted to empty which the job interpreted as "all".
- Corrective actions:
  * Hotfix: add explicit non-empty-scope guard and add unit test for tag renames.
  * Platform: add a safety throttle so a TTL job cannot evict >10% of prefixes in a single run without manual approval.
  * Customer mitigation: option to pin prefixes per-account for 24–72h after major control-plane operations.
- Communication: share postmortem with Cargofy and run a short AMA for customers on safety controls.

I've opened SUP-3219 for tracking. Once you all sign off I'll turn this into the external postmortem.

—Rishi

Marissa/Jonas — thank you. The proposed mitigations look good to us. We accept the recommended goodwill credit and appreciate the pinning option while we complete our release. Please include a note about monitoring improvements in the postmortem (we'd like to see synthetic checks for prefix churn).

We'll close this once we get the external postmortem and the credit applied.

Best — Priyanka
